sources_considered.why: Reports the first hands-on review of the December 2024 Sora release, which names object permanence.
OpenAI's own statement of the limitations of the released Sora.
A 2024 benchmark of several leading video models on physical commonsense.

receipt.public_excerpt: it suffers from the same flaws as other generative tools out there, namely issues related to object permanence. In Sora videos, objects pass in front of each other or behind each other in ways that don’t make sense, and disappear and reappear without any reason.

evidence_items.explanation: The first review of the December 2024 Sora release found object-permanence failures and called them the same flaws as other generative tools. This matches both the Sora part and the 'all models' part.

receipt.public_excerpt: The version of Sora we are deploying has many limitations. It often generates unrealistic physics and struggles with complex actions over long durations.

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI itself said the released Sora often generates unrealistic physics. This is consistent with continued physical-consistency problems.

receipt.public_excerpt: Our human evaluation reveals that the existing models severely lack the ability to generate videos adhering to the given text prompts, while also lack physical commonsense.

evidence_items.explanation: A 2024 benchmark of several open and closed video models found that even the best one followed physical laws in under 40% of cases. This supports the claim that such problems were widespread, though it measures physical commonsense broadly, not object permanence alone.

unresolved_gaps: No evaluation tests every video model specifically for object permanence. 'All models' is supported only for the leading models evaluated.
